_meta: iter 148: 🚧 Constraint-Shift Drill sidecar registry (5th sidecar bank after iter-79 complexity-claims / iter-86-87 idiom-pairs / iter-117 clarify-distractor-bank / iter-118 hotseat-followups). Each entry pairs a lesson with (a) its canonical's ORIGINAL constraint claim and (b) a SHIFTED constraint the user must satisfy. The drill: show canonical, prompt rewrite-to-shifted-claim, grade via runCode (output match) + structural-fingerprint regex that catches the canonical's antipattern (must NOT match in the user's submission for the shift to count). v1 ships 2 hand-validated entries spanning distinct shift types — data-structure swap (two-sum: hash → no-extra-DS) and allocation removal (valid-palindrome: string-alloc → in-place). Each entry hand-validated by (a) confirming the regex MATCHES the canonical (so grade would correctly reject canonical-as-is), (b) confirming a known-good shifted solution runs + produces expectedOutput AND does NOT trigger the regex. **iter-149 corpus expansion**: add entries where the regex can be made specific enough to avoid false-positives on the runner scaffold (the reverse-list iter↔recursion shift was deferred because `for`/`while` regex would catch the toList/toArr helpers; needs a more targeted regex like `curr.next = prev` antipattern). **First §9C ship ever.**

shifts.originalClaim: O(n) time, O(n) extra space (hash map for complement lookup)
shifts.shiftedClaim: O(1) extra space — no auxiliary Map / Set / Object / Array (allowed: O(n²) time)
shifts.hint: Without a hash map, you have to scan for the complement linearly. Two nested loops; outer fixes one element, inner finds its pair.
shifts.structuralCheckExplain: User submission must NOT use Map/Set or .set() — that's the canonical's O(n)-space technique, exactly the constraint we're shifting away from.

shifts.originalClaim: O(n) time, O(n) extra space (intermediate cleaned-string allocation)
shifts.shiftedClaim: O(1) extra space — no .replace, no .split, no new string — check alpha-numeric inline as you walk
shifts.hint: Two pointers from each end. Skip non-alphanumeric inline. Lowercase per-character (.toLowerCase() on a char is constant, not an allocation).
shifts.structuralCheckExplain: User submission must NOT use .replace() or .split() — those build new intermediate strings, exactly the O(n)-allocation we're shifting away from. Per-char .toLowerCase() is fine (constant, not allocation).

shifts.originalClaim: O(n) time, O(n) extra space (frequency Map of one string + decrement walk over the other)
shifts.shiftedClaim: No Map / Set / Object — sort both strings + compare. Trades O(n) → O(n log n) time for O(1) auxiliary structure (sort works in-place on the char array).
shifts.hint: If both strings sort to the same canonical form, they're anagrams. .split('') → .sort() → .join('') for each, then compare ===. No counter map needed.
shifts.structuralCheckExplain: User submission must NOT use Map/Set or .set() — that's the canonical's O(n)-space frequency-counter technique, exactly the constraint we're shifting away from. Sort-and-compare uses no auxiliary structures (the sorted array is throwaway temp).

shifts.originalClaim: Group via `new Map()` + .set/.get/.has (preserves insertion order; Map is the canonical bucket-by-fingerprint structure)
shifts.shiftedClaim: Use a plain JS Object as the bucket-by-fingerprint structure — no `new Map`. Object.values preserves insertion order for non-integer string keys (the sorted-char fingerprints are non-numeric, so order is preserved).
shifts.hint: const groups = {}; for each string, compute the sorted-char key; if !groups[key] init []; push. Return Object.values(groups). Same algorithm, plain-object container instead of Map — exercises the 'what if I don't have Map?' pivot every JS-1.5-era interviewer eventually asks.
shifts.structuralCheckExplain: User submission must NOT use `new Map(` — the shift requires reaching for a plain object as the bucket. Set is still allowed (different role; not the bucket). Object literal `{}` as bucket is the intended shifted pattern.
